newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korea's FKI upgrades 1997 GDP growth forecast.
newsitem.headline: S.Korea's FKI upgrades 1997 GDP growth forecast.

text.p: The Federation of Korean Industries (FKI) said on Thursday it had revised upward its forecast for this year's gross domestic product (GDP) growth to 5.9 percent from of 5.5 percent.
The FKI said in a report the revision was attributable to a better-than-expected performance in the first quarter and a fast recovery of exports, engine for the South Korean economy.

Although the continued slump in domestic consumption and investment is slowing import demand, the pace of recovery in exports is gaining heat due to the last year's slump and the appreciation of the Japanese yen, the report said.
The FKI, representing South Korea's big conglomerates or chaebol, forecast the GDP would grow by 5.3 percent in the first half and 6.4 percent in the second half.
The forecasts compared with a 4.8 percent growth for the first half and a 6.1 percent growth for the second half that the federation predicted in April.
The FKI revised downward its forecast for this year's current account deficit to $19.26 billion from its earlier forecast of a $20.95 billion shortfall.

It said the nation's exports were expected to grow by 12 percent while imports are seen expanding by 5.5 percent. Its earlier forecasts put the export growth at 11 percent and the import growth at 8.1 percent.
